CONTROLS

The controls for the following functions are located on the driver's door panel trim:

  • driver's window opening/closing;
  • passenger window opening/closing
  • exterior rear view mirror joystick.

The buttons for opening/closing the passenger window are located on the passenger door panel trim.

OPERATION

All the functions described here are managed by the two door control units and the luggage compartment control unit (for the rear doors)See descriptions 5505 INSTRUMENT/GAUGE ELECTRICAL CIRCUITS

Door locking / unlocking

The simultaneous operation of the two door locks takes place via:

  • the TEG remote control;
  • the locking/unlocking button in the centre console.

The TEG remote has 3 buttons which allow the operation of the central locking system: a button for unlocking the doors, one for locking the vehicle and one for releasing the boot.

See descriptions 5520 ENGINE STARTING

The fuel flap is locked/unlocked together with the doors.

If the remote control fails, insert the metal insert (inside the key) in the lock in the driver's door and turn it.With the central locking on, pulling the interior opening lever for one of the doors causes the closure for all the doors to be released. If there is no electrical power supply the doors can be locked manually

The locks have an additional motor that carries out the dead lock function which allows the interior door opening handles to be mechanically disconnected so that it is no longer possible to open the door from the inside (for example, after having broken the glass in a theft attempt); the dead lock function also inhibits the operation of the door locking/unlocking buttons in the dashboard.

The dead lock function is switched on at the time the doors are locked or by pressing the remote control twice.

The LED in the driver's door produces the following signals:

  • Locking the locks: the LED lights up for 3 seconds. If some of the doors or the boot are not properly shut at the time when the locks are locked, the LED flashes at 3 Hz for 3 seconds;
  • Dead lock activation: the LED flashes twice for 0.5 seconds;
  • Unlocking the locks: the LED goes out.

The doors are automatically unlocked if the inertia switch is operated: the instrument panel receives a signal from the switch, lights up the appropriate warning light and notifies the Body Computer via the CAN.

Possible adjustments

It is possible, using the special setup in the instrument panel, to select whether to unlock all the doors or only the driver's front door, whilst all the other doors and the boot remain locked.

It is possible to enable/disable the locking of the doors above a certain speed threshold (20 km/h) using the special setup in the instrument panel: in this case the Body Computer implements the locking of the doors when this threshold is exceeded.

When the speed returns below this level, the doors and the boot remain locked; later on, when one of the doors is opened, the function is re-enabled and, if the threshold is exceeded, the doors are locked once again.

The boot unlocking operating mode can be selected still using the special setup in the instrument panel:

- assisted boot unlocking: the rear boot is considered as a fifth door to all intents and purposes;

- independent boot unlocking: the boot is locked when the doors are locked, whilst it can be unlocked independently of the unlocking of the doors.

Electric windows

The electric windows for the front doors are operated through the switches on the driver's door (both windows) and the passenger side (passenger side only).

Automatic operation takes place as follows:

  • if the button is pressed is between 60 and 300 milliseconds, operation is manual: the glass goes up/down only with the key pressed;
  • f the key is pressed for longer than 300 milliseconds, operation is automatic: even if the button is released, the glass continues to move up/down until the end of travel position is reached or until the intervention of the anti-crush safety system (if fitted);
  • pressing the button again whilst the window is moving stops it in the position it is in;
  • if the button is pressed for less than 60 milliseconds, this is ignored (it is treated as an accidental knock).

The windows are automatically opened or closed through the special prolonged (more than 2 seconds) command sent by the TEG remote control button.

Short drop function

When the doors are opened (whether with key-on or key-off status), the door nodes implement the short drop function to prevent interference between the windows and the roof or the hood.

The short drop position is set at 10 mm from the window full closure position.

In detail: when the door is opened if the window is closing, this takes place until the Short Drop position is reached and NOT until it is completely shut. If the position of one or both of the windows is the same as the Short Drop position, no automatic movement will take place.

If the door is open, the windows can be moved manually either downwards or upwards in the space between the "window completely open" and "Short Drop" positions and therefore the window cannot be completely closed.

When the door is closed, the windows stopped in the Short Drop position are completely closed automatically.

Middle drop function (spider version only)

If there is a request to open/close the Hood, the door nodes activate the Middle Drop function:

Following the request for the hood opening or closing cycle, the windows are lowered to prevent interference with the movement of the hood; the Middle Drop position is fixed at 50 mm from the position where the windows are completely closed.

On the command to open or close the hood using the dedicated button (see DF 7030H) and in key-on conditions, the hood control node sends a signal to start the opening cycle: if the windows are in the "completely closed" position on in an intermediate position between "completely closed" and Middle Drop, the door nodes activate the movement of the windows until they reach the Middle Drop position.

When the Middle Drop position is reached, the door nodes send suitable signals allowing the hydraulic movement of the Hood.

If the position of one or both of the windows is the same as the Middle Drop position or they are in the position between "completely open" and Middle Drop, no automatic movement takes place.

If the window raising controls are pressed during the movement of the hood and the glass is in the Middle Drop position, they are ignored and the Middle Drop position is maintained.

If, on the other hand, the window is in a position between "completely open" and Middle Drop it is possible to raise the window until it reaches the Middle Drop position.

The windows can always be lowered with the Hood in any position.

Behaviour if the hood is faulty.

In this situation the door nodes exclude the automatic middle drop function, in other words when the fault appears the glass can move freely in the range between "completely open" and "completely closed" if the door is closed or in the range between "completely open" and "short drop" if the door is open.

Window movement interruption

The door nodes should interrupt the operation of the window in the following cases:

- when automatic movement is in progress and either the up or down control is pressed;

- at the top or bottom end of travel in both manual or automatic mode;

- when the window is in the process of closing and the Short Drop position has been exceeded and the door is opened at the same time. After the window is placed in the Short Drop position when the door is closed, the window is closed as far as the top end of travel position.

Anti-crush safety function

Each control unit in the door also manages the anti-crush safety function: it acquires information concerning the possible presence of an obstacle whilst the glass is closing: under these circumstances the control unit immediately interrupts the travel of the window and reverses it to the lower end of travel position.

If a failure is detected in the system or if the anti-crush safety function is activated 3 times in the space of 1 minute or if there is a failure, the system automatically enters into recovery mode (self-protection).This condition is evident from the window closing by being raised in stages.

If this happens the system restoral procedure must be carried out as follows:

  • work with the doors closed and the windows closed, as well as the hood closed - on the Spider version;
  • completely open the driver's door window keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position;
  • completely close the driver's door window keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position;
  • proceed in the same way for the passenger window as well;
  • make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work correctly in automatic mode.

Following no power supply to the control units (e.g. battery disconnected) the system must be "initialized" once again following the procedure described above.

Rear view mirror adjustment

The door mirrors can be electrically adjusted in two directions using a joystick control located in the door controls on the driver's side: a selection cursor makes it possible to choose either the left or the right mirror.

The button controls two electrical motors located in each of the two mirrors: one motor allows the rotation of the mirror on the horizontal axis, another on the vertical axis.

Another button controls the folding back of the mirrors if required (for example when trying to get through a narrow space).

In addition to moving the door mirrors manually, it is possible to memorize and later on recall 3 positions defined in relation to the position of the driver's seat; the passenger side rear view mirror is also positioned automatically when reverse gear is engaged.
